reviews.text:
I visited Gangnam because I had an appointment with a friend, and it was more delicious than I expected.
I ordered plenty of jjaggeul and Jeolla-do style red pepper paste pork rice bowl, and I was satisfied with both as they were the best menu items.
The soup was thick and went well with rice, and the red pepper paste pork rice bowl was a dish that I kept coming back to because the spicy and sweet seasoning blended well.
The portions were generous and the side dishes were good, so it was nice to have a filling meal.
This is a place I want to visit again when I crave Korean or spicy food in Gangnam.

reviews.author: GGG
reviews.text: It is right in front of Exit 3 of Gangnam Station, so it is easily accessible, and the atmosphere is unique as it has a traditional Hanok interior and even a watermill. The Jeonju bibimbap was seasoned just right and the portion was generous, and the gochujang pork rice bowl was deliciously spicy, just like Jeolla-do style. It comes with a generous amount of steamed egg and goes well with the spicy rice bowl. It's easy to eat alone, and there are rooms for 6 to 7 people, so I think it would be good for a team dinner. This is a place I'll come back to again when I'm craving Korean food.

I visited because I wanted to eat a hearty, comforting meal near Gangnam Station, and it was a choice I had no regrets about. I liked the clean and cozy wood-toned interior that felt as soon as I entered the store, and the friendly staff welcomed me so I was able to have a pleasant meal.
​I was impressed by the owner's hospitality because the generously savory dish I ordered, as the name suggests, had plenty of ingredients such as meat and kimchi. The soup was thick and thick, so I mixed it with white rice and ate it, so there was literally nothing left to eat. I felt my stomach relax because the deep flavor of the ingredients came through rather than the taste of artificial seasoning.

I felt like I was being treated well as the food was neatly presented on a tray and the side dishes went well with the main menu. The store is structured so that people can eat comfortably by themselves, making it a sacred place for those looking for a good place to eat alone at Gangnam Station. It was great to be able to conveniently order through the kiosk and eat without worrying about what was going on.

reviews.author: Zabaroo
reviews.text:
This restaurant focuses on Korean cuisine, cold noodles, and makguksu (buckwheat noodles). It feels a bit similar to Woorae-ok, but the drawback is that the price is similar to Woorae-ok.
The food was good overall, but you should keep in mind that the prices are quite high, perhaps because it is located in the office workers' street of Gangnam Station.
Even though the marbled pork is made from Korean beef, it was boiled gently and not greasy. However, I feel that the quantity is a bit small compared to the price of 65,000 won.
Potato pancake is a dish made with whole potatoes sliced ​​and pan-fried. Personally, I think the potato pancake made with sliced ​​or grated potatoes is better.
A surprisingly delicious menu item was the kimchi dumplings. The dumpling filling was quite substantial and the kimchi and meat went well together. The dumplings themselves were delicious, but frying them made them even more delicious.
Pyeongyang naengmyeon is made in the Wooraeok style and has a strong meaty flavor, so it is relatively easy for even beginners to Pyongyang naengmyeon to enjoy. The bibim makguksu was delicious and not too sweet, but it was a bit spicy so keep that in mind.

reviews.author: Chaebin Kim
reviews.text:
I ate Pyeongyang cold noodles and dumplings.

hmm… First of all, the atmosphere is a little different from what I expected. Rather than a Pyongyang naengmyeon restaurant, it feels more like a bar serving Pyongyang naengmyeon and fish belly trays. Whiskey, champagne, wine, etc… They sell alcohol worth hundreds of thousands of won and also sell various snacks. Actually, in this respect, the atmosphere is a bit... It sucks.

If you think about the taste of Pyongyang Naengmyeon, it is a spicy-tasting naengmyeon that, like Woorae-ok, is likely to be enjoyed by first-time eaters. Rich and spicy flavor. As I ate it, I got a strong taste of cinnamon or ginger at the end. The decoration is one piece each of pork and beef, but the texture or something like that is a bit ambiguous... do.

The dumplings were just so-so. It was cooked well, but the taste was so-so.

I don’t know if I’ll go back to eat Pyongyang naengmyeon again.

reviews.author: EUNJEONG LEE
reviews.text:
Visited on July 8, 2021

This is a meat restaurant located in a two-story building near Gangnam Station.
An acquaintance offered to buy it, so I got it.
Since it is a restaurant specializing in aged sirloin located in Gangnam, the prices are a bit steep, but after tasting the staff's service, meat, and meal menu, I thought it was worth the price.

The side dishes mainly consisted of vegetables, so it was great to eat with meat.
The meat was so delicious that it melted in my mouth.

I also remember the fried rice I ate at the end. It's a place you'll want to visit again for a treat with an acquaintance or on a special anniversary.

reviews.text: I had rib bomb rice and braised pork belly with kimchi for lunch, and both were okay! Both have ribs/pork belly and kimchi stew on top of rice, and the portions are quite large. Is 1.5 servings enough for an adult woman like me? It's a bit annoying to eat rib bomb rice by cutting off the ribs with scissors ^^; It’s a sweet soy sauce/onion seasoning.

reviews.author: GTOURER
reviews.text: As the name suggests, they sell honest, top-grade beef sirloin/tenderloin/t-bone steak. The sirloin tenderloin costs 42,000 and 44,000/150g respectively, which is an acceptable price considering the location, interior, and meat quality. I didn't order the T-bone steak, but it was about 860g for 140,000 won, and except for the bone weight, it seemed similar to the price at a high-end restaurant. The quality of the meat, the quality of the side dishes, and the interior design were all luxurious and clean, so there were no complaints, but I was embarrassed that I had to grill the meat myself in a restaurant of this caliber. As it is good meat, we expect it to be even more perfect if it is grilled by a skilled person and served with the best taste.

reviews.text:
Originally, this place changed frequently.
I think I found a landlord who will stay for a long time.

Meals are served at a table setting and bottled water is served.
It costs 8,000 to 9,000 won per person and you have to wait in line during lunch.
There is a steady flow of customers even in the evening.
The main characteristic is that it is cooked without adding any seasoning.
Bibimbap and soybean paste stew are made with soybean paste as the base and contain radish radish and young radish, and pork belly is added.
Although the seasoning is weak, the meat is delicious with stew and pork belly.
Harmonizes and brings out the taste

I think three young people came together.

reviews.author: Dongmin Lee
reviews.text:
It may not be bad value for money, but it's not particularly delicious either.
First of all, bibimbap, soybean paste stew, and pork belly side dishes come as a set, but I don't know when Korea started counting kkakdugi as a side dish.
And the brisket soybean paste stew is really tasteless. I think they just added beef brisket to the boiled soybean paste stew, and although there was a lot of brisket, it had a tasteless flavor unique to the beef. Moreover, it does not taste like Korean soybean paste stew and is slightly bland.

reviews.author: Inyoung Kim

However, the bibimbap with stir-fried perilla seeds was good, but it felt a bit overcooked. I think it would be better if you added a little more texture.
A fried egg was also added, and the marbled beef stew that came with it was delicious because it had a lot of marble and was refreshing. Because it was made in an earthen pot, it stayed hot until the end of the meal.
The spacing between tables is narrow, but it seems unavoidable in Gangnam.
It's a good place to eat alone.
